once.prompt: Priya needs the Halden Biopharma proposal by Friday 6 November: six new waste streams from their Caldwell Bend plant, 4,860 tons a year from February 2027, three-year contract. Characterise and classify each stream, work out which of our units can take it under its permit, its capacity and Halden's destruction requirement, cost every route and price it from the price book, test the margin against the floor, and draft the acceptance memo, the quote letter and the pricing schedule in the Delmar structure. Attached: the six profiles and the Delmar pricing schedule.

reads.res: Six profiles, 4,860 tons a year: process wastewater, solvent, expired product, aerosols, product-contact solids, scrubber water · EPA identification number not yet issued
Contract summary, streams and routing, price and full cost, capacity and fallback, approvals, evidence: the structure approved in 2023
All six results released 29 October · H2 halogens 3.2% · permitted units for every code
Port Terrell 94% booked for the fourth quarter, no first-quarter plan · Granger 71% · 2026 prices and the Caldwell Bend lanes
Product-contact waste incinerated with a certificate of destruction per shipment; deep well, landfill and discharge treatment not acceptable
Priya: quote by Friday in the Delmar structure · Dana: Granger unless Port Terrell publishes a plan · Raj: the floor at the quoted routing, new Texas fee
A permitted code is not an outlet without capacity · a requirement binds the routing · margin on the route the stream will take · no stream below 15%

questions.title: Port Terrell is the closest incinerator and the cheapest route, but its capacity is not confirmed: where are the three QR-14 streams quoted?
questions.text: Port Terrell is 140 miles from Caldwell Bend against 1020 to Granger, and the quote earns 43.0% there against 34.7% on Granger. It is 94% booked for the fourth quarter, has no first-quarter plan, the committee ruled out new pharmaceutical volume there until the plan is out, and the kiln is down today.

questions.title: How is the destruction requirement met for the process wastewater?
questions.text: QR-14 asks for destruction with a certificate per shipment. Incineration meets it. Bayou Verde deep well is permitted for the codes and is the cheapest route ($117.58 a ton against $474.14 at Granger), but it is disposal under the UIC permit, not destruction, and Halden's quality team rejected it twice.

tiles.s: A certificate of destruction per shipment

tiles.t: Offer deep well as an alternative line
tiles.s: The quote falls to $2.08M; does not meet QR-14

tiles.t: Incineration, with deep well shown beside it

nodes.title: Characterise and classify the six streams
nodes.purpose: What each stream is, its codes, what the laboratory found, and what the customer requires of it.
nodes.how: Profiles against the released results; RCRA and state codes, DOT description and the LDR standard per stream; QR-14 read against each stream; anything the profile did not say flagged.
nodes.check: Every stream has released results; every requirement is quoted from the document.

nodes.title: Check the network: permits, capacity and the fallback for each stream
nodes.purpose: Which units may take each stream, which have capacity when it arrives, and what happens if the named unit is unavailable.
nodes.how: Permitted codes by unit; fourth-quarter bookings and the first-quarter plans; the halogen limits; Tidewater's renewal; Port Terrell's outage. A permitted code is not an outlet without capacity.
nodes.check: Every unit named has the codes on its permit and capacity in the bookings.

nodes.title: Cost every route and price each stream from the book
nodes.purpose: Full cost a ton at every eligible unit, the book price, and the margin per stream and for the contract.
nodes.how: Treatment plus handling plus the receiving state's fee (from 1 November) plus the Caldwell Bend lane; price from the 2026 book; margin per stream against 15% and for the contract against 28%, at the routing agreed.
nodes.check: Every stream's margin recomputes from tons, price and full cost; the contract margin foots.

nodes.title: Confirm where the QR-14 streams are quoted
nodes.purpose: Stops here and asks you before the routing is priced into the quote.
nodes.how: Port Terrell is cheaper and closer and its capacity is not confirmed; Granger has the capacity and the longer haul. The quote and the memo rest on this, and only you can confirm it.
nodes.check: Your answer is recorded on the plan before anything after it runs.

nodes.title: Check acceptance and what has to be in place before the first shipment
nodes.purpose: Whether every stream is acceptable under the policy, and the gaps to close before 1 January.
nodes.how: Each stream against the acceptance policy: understood, permitted, capacity, requirement met; the generator's EPA identification number; the approval level; the chemist's review at each receiving unit.
nodes.check: Every stream is acceptable, or the gap is named with who closes it.

nodes.title: Three ways to quote
nodes.purpose: One quote to put to Priya and Marcus, with what it trades off.
nodes.how: Weigh the quote on Granger with Port Terrell as the alternative against the quote on Port Terrell, and against declining the process water and quoting the other five; state each trade-off and every caveat that reached it.
nodes.check: The recommendation names its remaining caveats and the alternatives it rejected.

summary: Read the six profiles against the released results. 4,860 tons a year; every stream is understood and every result was released on 29 October. Three streams carry QR-14 (process wastewater, expired product, product-contact solids): destruction with a certificate per shipment, so deep well, landfill and discharge treatment are not outlets for them.

One finding the profile did not say: the solvent waste carries 3.2% total halogens from a chlorinated intermediate, above Fox Hollow's 2.0% fuel blending limit. The scrubber water is D002 at pH 12.6; the process water is not ignitable (3.8% methanol) and carries 40 mg/L of active ingredient, so aqueous treatment is not an outlet for it.

summary: Every stream has a permitted unit with capacity, and the three QR-14 streams have two: Granger and Port Terrell. Port Terrell is 94.4% booked on aqueous incineration for the fourth quarter, has no first-quarter plan, and its kiln is down since 3 November; Granger is 70.9% booked with about 2,175 tons of first-quarter headroom against 725 tons of process water a quarter.

The solvent cannot go to Fox Hollow (halogens); Tidewater fuel blending is permitted but under renewal until 18 December and earns nothing from Texas. Aerosols go to Cypress Landing (38.1% booked); the scrubber water to Bayou Verde deep well (56.7%). The committee ruled out new pharmaceutical volume on Port Terrell until its plan is published.
